lines.en: We move closer to the water, but not close enough for it to catch us too.
Part of me wishes that it would — but that the water would bend in a way that spares the girl beside me so I can witness its tidal wrath in a manner that renders me permanently breathless.
Suffice it to say, I’d take that over her and everyone else always emptying out my lungs.
Even when it’s quiet like this, when our minds are both so obviously elsewhere, I’m always aware.
Of how easily she could suffocate me...
Of how her hands, clasped tightly around her knees, feel more like they’re curled around my neck. And how fighting a war against myself has made me too exhausted to even ask her to stop.
: Well...looks like it’s just you and me again.
: Guess so.
: You worried too?
: They’ll figure it out.
: I think so too.
: I’m sure it’ll happen if we just keep telling ourselves that.
: It’s typically the opposite in my experience.
: Yeah...same.
: Maybe we should keep telling ourselves that they’re going to break up then? If fate and hope and all those other vague, optimistic adjectives are so commonly in disagreement with us, I mean.
: I think doing that would just make us bad friends.
: True...
: Guess we’re kind of fucked either way then, huh?
: Guess so. But at the end of the day, it’s those two who are way more fucked than either of us right now. We’re only fucked by-proxy.
: Well, hey. I’d take that over not getting fucked at all, if you know what I mean.
: Uhh...just to clarify, that was supposed to be more of a joke than one more act of pressuring you into screwing me. Just...trying to lighten the mood.
: I know. Plus, even if I did take that the wrong way, you’d get to fall back on the excuse of being drunk. You can’t lose.
: I guess I am a little tipsy, yeah. I was kind of just hamming it up for Wakana’s sake, though.
: You felt it too, right? How...I don’t know...fragile she seemed?
: I’m not sure I would have if you didn’t point something out when we first got here. She’s even better at hiding her feelings than I am and I’ve essentially built my entire character around that.
: Well, yeah. You two are really similar.
: Talented, gloomy intellectuals who make it hard for you to get close to them...but also the type of people who will silently cherish you for the rest of your life whether you want them to or not.
: I wish I met you sooner. Both of you. I’d have loved having people like that growing up.
: How are you doing, Senpai? Like...really doing?
: I’m not really sure.
: “Confused” is probably the best word right now.
: About what?
: It’s hard to say. Leaving the house is like playing a game of roulette at this point.

: Sometimes, something good will happen. Sometimes, something terrible. But it’s those terrible days I focus on the most because there’s like a...voice in the back of my mind telling me that’s what I deserve.
: At the same time, though, I’m trying to change for Ami’s sake. And that’s...hard. I’m not good when it comes to changing.
: For what it’s worth, Senpai...I think you’ve changed a lot since you left school. It’s not normal for you to just tell me things without putting up some sort of fight first.
: I don’t have the energy to fight anymore. All I want to do is sleep.
: Senpai. Look at me for a second.
: I got you.
: Okay?
: I know...
: Everyone does.
: Yeah, but I’m not everyone. I’m your loyal kouhai and best friend who can be anything you need her to be. Just say the word and I’ll do it.
: Imani-
: Need some cash for dinner? I got you. Someone to walk the dog you don’t have? Again, I got you.
: Imani-
: Quickie in the closet before class? I got you, man.
: Imani, can I ask you something?
: Of course, Senpai. You can ask me anything.
: Why don’t you ever wear a swimsuit?
: Is...that really relevant right now? I thought you were in the process of like, telling me about your feelings and stuff?
: Then I feel like there’s a part of you I’m still missing — something you’re not telling me because you’re worried of how I’ll react. And I don’t think that’s really fair.
: I mean...how is it unfair? You do the same shit, Senpai.
: I know...I have a lot to work on.
: But I want to tell you all of those things because I want you to understand the type of person you are to me. I want to be a better friend. I just...haven’t figured out how yet.
: Well, it’s the same for me...Just my thing doesn’t really have anything to do with our friendship.
: Of course it does. Not telling me shows that you don’t fully trust me.
: Trust doesn’t have anything to do with it, okay? I know you won’t think any differently of me. I’m just...embarrassed, I guess. Or maybe, like...ashamed? I don’t know.
: I don’t like swimsuits. I don’t like...revealing myself.
: And I don’t like voicing my problems to people but that’s practically all I’ve been doing lately.
: Also, you’d kind of have to reveal your body to me if we ever had sex. So...there’s that.
: Not if we keep the lights off!~
: But also, if we kept the lights off, you might not be able to find me at all and would wind up fucking my couch or something. Which would be wild since I don’t even have a couch.
: Hah...
: Okay...I’ll tell you.
: But I have a condition.
: And what’s that?
: You can’t say anything.
: I’m not going to tell anyone, Imani. I-
: No- I don’t mean it like that, Senpai. I mean...I want you to just...sit there and listen. No sympathy or...encouragement or...anything like that. I just want to get it over with.
Imani gets up and heads over to where the water meets the land.
The moonlight accentuates her beauty, but I know it’s fleeting as I can tell that she is about to do everything in her power to cast one more shadow on it.
: I’ll also be expecting at least one deep, dark secret from you in return. Got it?
: You mean one you haven’t probably already heard from Wakana and Osako?
: Senpai, I-
: No. If I’m not going to comment on your thing, you’re not going to comment on mine. That’s my condition.
: Mm...okay. Fair enough.
: Welcome to Imani Imai’s impromptu story time...she says, pretending to have not rehearsed this conversation a hundred times already.
: So, you may not have noticed this as it’s really hard to pick up on, but I’m actually black.
: What? Really?
: Shush. No jokes either. Let me use them all to clear the air.
: So yes, in a shocking turn of events, I am black. But, as I’ve mentioned in the past, I’m half-Japanese as well.
: A bastard child, if you will. A product of my mother’s infidelity and the insatiable lust of a foreign tourist who didn’t know how to pull out on time.
: Despite all of that, though...despite knowing that none of his blood flowed within me, my father raised me as if I was his own.
: He taught me about God....How all men and women are created equal and how each and every one of them is deserving of love. And that really stuck with me. Sans the God part.
: I just wish it stuck with his other children.
: You see...they never saw me the way he did. And they spared no effort at all in reminding me of that every chance they got. All behind the scenes, though. At least at first.
: It was only a matter of time until everyone in school knew what I really was. Which meant it was only a matter of time until my mother started getting shit as well. And rightly so, might I add.
: You know, the only way I’ve ever really related to her at all was in the fact that we were both relentlessly trashed by our peers over a one night stand she made.
: Just I wasn’t really there to do anything about it on account of still being a little Japanese tadpole at the time.
: But regardless, I was bullied. She was bullied. And every day, my father would pull me aside and reassure me that this was only temporary.
: That I was the same as everyone else and that they would all see that one day.
: So I’d smile. Tell him I love him — which I did. I loved him so much. And in hindsight, he’s probably the only thing that kept me going.
: It started off with just name calling. Sansa ni...idiot. Ko’hweni...useless. Ahbwah...animal. Ashawo...whore.
: And my personal favorite, ching chong fuo, which is a Twi slur for the Chinese. Fucking morons didn’t even know what type of Asian I was.
: Ignoring insults is easy, though. So I focused more on educating myself than giving into all of the bullying since I wanted to make my father proud.
: But, here’s a thing I wish I knew sooner.
: Bullies really don’t like it when you’re smart.
: One day, a bunch of kids from my school got together for a party to celebrate the end of the year. And, being the stupid and fearless specimen I am, I decided to go check it out.
: I mean, it wasn’t like I didn’t have any friends. There were a handful who’d stick up for me from time to time before tapering off from the consequent ostracization they’d receive in return.
: So I found a few of them, got some food, got some drinks...started talking. And then there was this boy who came up to me.
: His name was Kwesi — popular kid. Some relation to the mayor or...some other comparable noteworthy position like that. And we started talking.
: He told me how beautiful my eyes were...refilled my drinks and wound up buying me dessert from some stall not far from where all of us were hanging out.
: He seemed nice. And it was a party, so I thought...what the hell? I’m gonna let this guy run some bases.
: I’d already messed around with some other boys by then, so it’s not like I was totally inexperienced or anything.
: So he takes me back to his place, right? Really nice house up on a hill that overlooked the rest of the village. I still remember how beautiful the lights were from the window of his bedroom.
: Unfortunately, that memory is somewhat soiled for me by what comes after.
: Which brings us back to the main question. Why don’t I ever wear a swimsuit? And unfortunately, the answer kind of sucks.
: Kwesi tied me up. I agreed, thinking it might be fun. But I probably wouldn’t have agreed had I known that he would subsequently invite another six of his friends into the room.
: One of them was my brother.
: And so I immediately looked at him with tears welling up in my eyes, knowing that there was no way in hell that this wasn’t going to end horribly for me. But that motherfucker just looked away...
: They used scissors to cut off my clothes...wrote some things on my body I never bothered looking at since I’d already heard every insult possible by then. But that was just the beginning.
: And leaving out the middle part, which I’m not going to burden you with, all that’s left is the grand finale.
: And the reason I like it best in the dark.
: One of Kwesi’s friends boiled some water. A lot of it. Can’t remember why specifically, but I think it had something to do with not being able to get the writing off.
: They threw it at me. Several pots worth, to be exact. One boy even used an electric kettle. Like, for real man?
: And yeah! Turns out the human body handles boiling water just as well as you’d expect it to. And the evidence of that is written all over me.
: It wasn’t until the damage had already been done that they realized they’d gone too far. Well...one of them, at least.
: Maybe the words of my father just took a little longer to reach him than they should have, but my brother eventually ran off to call for help.
: I spent three weeks in the hospital after that. And while I don’t look nearly as bad now as I did the first few years, I still can’t look at myself without thinking of what happened that night.
: At least one good thing came of it, though.
: When school started the next year...no one ever bullied me again.
: Thank you for remaining quiet and not battering me with sympathy. I appreciate it.
: May I speak now?
: Yes, Senpai. You may speak.
: Did you bring it with you?
: Yes...
: Can you show me?
: Yes...
